title: Istanbul, Kuwait and the 1976 tour with Benny Carter
summary: He recalls the Bicentennial tour with Benny Carter and Morroe Berger.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Kuwait? Well, I had a good time there.

I had a good time there in Kuwait. Yeah, I had a nice time in Kuwait. And I had a nice time in Istanbul. I went over there with Benny Carter in 1976 I think it was…the Bicentennial. I was with your father.
That’s how I got to know you.

Yeah (laughs). He used to come and say, “Sweets, talk to me.” I’d say, “Well, what the hell you want to know about Morroe?” “Tell me something I can go back home and say.” And I liked a fellow over there, he’s a drummer, and he came to see the concert because he had a band on a television show. I still see him.
I think his name was Tuna Otenel or something like that?
I can’t think of it, but I see him every time I go—he brings back the memories of when I was first over there. I had a good time with him.
From what I heard of the impression you made on that tour, I thought it would solve all the problems of the Middle East.
No, it just started it (laughs). That was just great…to be walking around the pyramids, what an experience.
